items.exampleEn: The old poem expresses the writer's grief at leaving his home country.
items.exampleZh: 那首古詩表達了作者離開故鄉的悲痛。

items.exampleEn: Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity.
items.exampleZh: 每個人都應該受到有尊嚴的對待。

items.exampleEn: His grin told me he had good news.
items.exampleZh: 看他咧嘴一笑，我就知道他有好消息。

items.exampleEn: Baby turtles find their way to the sea by instinct.
items.exampleZh: 小海龜靠本能找到通往大海的路。

items.exampleEn: The shop cheated tourists by charging them double.
items.exampleZh: 那家店向觀光客收雙倍價錢，欺騙他們。

items.exampleEn: The team played desperately in the last few minutes.
items.exampleZh: 最後幾分鐘，球隊拚命地踢球。

items.exampleEn: I did my best, so I can sleep with a clear conscience.
items.exampleZh: 我已經盡力了，所以能問心無愧地好好睡一覺。

items.exampleEn: I made a dumb mistake and sent the email to the wrong person.
items.exampleZh: 我犯了一個蠢錯誤，把電子郵件寄給錯的人。

items.sentenceEn: Music can help people through times of grief.
items.sentenceZh: 音樂能幫助人們度過悲傷的時刻。

items.audioEn: If anyone cheats in this game, they will have to leave the table.
items.audioZh: 這個遊戲如果有人作弊，就得離開牌桌。
items.questionZh: 玩這個遊戲時作弊會怎樣？
options: The player loses one point each time
The player pays a small fine

items.sentenceEn: Animals know by instinct when danger is near.
items.sentenceZh: 動物憑本能就知道危險何時靠近。

items.sentenceEn: The cat was desperately trying to catch the bird.
items.sentenceZh: 那隻貓拚命想抓到那隻鳥。

items.stemEn: He has a guilty ____ because he told his best friend a lie.
items.stemZh: 他因為對最好的朋友說謊而良心不安。

items.stemEn: Even after losing his job, he kept his ____ and never complained.
items.stemZh: 即使丟了工作，他仍保持尊嚴，從不抱怨。

items.passageEn: Last week, Tom found a wallet full of cash on the bus. His first instinct was to keep it, because he desperately needed money for his rent. But his conscience would not let him. He was reluctant at first, but he finally called the owner, an old man who had spent all morning looking for it. When Tom returned the wallet, the man's face broke into a huge grin. He offered Tom a reward, but Tom refused, saying that taking money for doing the right thing would feel wrong. "You are an honest young man," the man said. Tom later laughed that keeping the money would have been a dumb idea anyway, since the man lived next door.
items.passageZh: 上週，Tom 在公車上撿到一個裝滿現金的錢包。他的第一個念頭是留下來，因為他急需錢付房租。但他的良心不允許。他一開始有點猶豫，最後還是打電話給失主，一位找了一整個早上的老先生。Tom 把錢包還給他時，老先生臉上露出大大的笑容。他想給 Tom 一筆謝禮，但 Tom 拒絕了，說做了對的事還收錢，感覺不對。老先生說：「你是個誠實的年輕人。」Tom 後來笑說，反正把錢留下來也是個蠢主意，因為那位老先生就住在他家隔壁。

questions.questionZh: Tom 一開始的直覺是什麼？

options: 覺得對方給的謝禮實在太少了

referenceEn: Cheating on an exam is wrong.

referenceEn: My son came home with a big grin because he got a good grade.
The old man gave me a friendly grin when I helped him.
rubricZh: 句子要用到 grin，當名詞（a big grin）或動詞（grin at…）都可以
